How it was scored

  • Scanned with OpenSCAP in the image build on 2026-10-20 21:10 UTC.
  • Content: SCAP Security Guide 0.1.82, profile “DISA STIG for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8” (xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_stig), with the refined value listed below.
  • Score = rules passed ÷ (rules passed + rules failed). Every rule listed under Exemptions failed in the scan and counts as a failure in the score. Not-applicable and not-checked rules are not scored.
  • This image runs AlmaLinux 8, not Red Hat Enterprise Linux. Red Hat does not provide, support or endorse it.
  • AlmaLinux is scored with the SCAP Security Guide content for Red Hat Enterprise Linux, so the checks that only Red Hat Enterprise Linux can pass appear as exemptions below.
  • The build's OpenSCAP gate was enforced: floor 90%, and no failing rule without a documented exemption.
  • FIPS mode is enabled, using the OS vendor's FIPS cryptographic modules.

An OpenSCAP score measures this image against SSG content. It is not a certification, authorization or accreditation, and it is not an assessment of your system.

Exemptions (16)

Each rule below fails in the image for the reason given, and the last column is what you do to meet it on your instance. The reasons and actions come from the build record (the signed POA&M lists the same rules).

RuleSTIG IDCategoryWhy it fails in the imageWhat you do
grub2_uefi_admin_username
Set the UEFI Boot Loader Admin Username to a Non-Default Value		RHEL-08-010141AWS Marketplace policy: you complete it after launchAWS Marketplace policy prohibits meeting this rule in an AMI: "AMI must not contain hardcoded secrets such as system user and service passwords (including hashed passwords)" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/product-and-ami-policies.html). A GRUB superuser only protects the boot loader together with its password hash, which cannot ship in the image.After launch run sudo stigready-set-credentials (installed in the image): it sets your own GRUB superuser and password in the RHEL 8 UEFI grub.cfg, which meets this rule on your instance.
grub2_uefi_password
Set the UEFI Boot Loader Password		RHEL-08-010140AWS Marketplace policy: you complete it after launchAWS Marketplace policy prohibits meeting this rule in an AMI: "AMI must not contain hardcoded secrets such as system user and service passwords (including hashed passwords)" and "Password-based authentication for instance services is prohibited. This applies even if the password is generated, reset, or defined by the user at launch"; Linux AMIs "must allow users to get fully privileged access (for example, to allow sudo access)" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/product-and-ami-policies.html). The rule needs a boot loader or root password hash in the image, or a sudo password for the key-only default user.After launch run sudo stigready-set-credentials (installed in the image): it sets your own GRUB superuser and password, root password and a sudo password for your admin user, and removes NOPASSWD, which meets this rule on your instance.

The rule needs a boot loader or root password hash in the image, or a sudo password for the key-only default user.After launch run sudo stigready-set-credentials (installed in the image): it sets your own GRUB superuser and password, root password and a sudo password for your admin user, and removes NOPASSWD, which meets this rule on your instance.
ensure_redhat_gpgkey_installed
Ensure Red Hat GPG Key Installed		no STIG ID in the build recordCheck names Red Hat: cannot apply to this distributionThe check passes only when the OS is RHEL and Red Hat's own signing keys are installed (gpg-pubkey-fd431d51, the Red Hat release key, plus that release's auxiliary key). Rocky Linux and AlmaLinux sign their packages with their own release keys, so no derivative image can carry Red Hat's key honestly. What the rule protects -- packages are only installed when their signature verifies against the distribution's key -- is still enforced and scored on these images by ensure_gpgcheck_globally_activated and ensure_gpgcheck_never_disabled (and ensure_gpgcheck_local_packages on STIG), which pass.None. The distribution's own key (RPM-GPG-KEY-Rocky-N or RPM-GPG-KEY-AlmaLinux-N) is installed and gpgcheck is on for every repository. If your accreditation requires Red Hat-signed packages, use the RHEL image.
installed_OS_is_vendor_supported
The Installed Operating System Is Vendor Supported		no STIG ID in the build recordCheck names Red Hat: cannot apply to this distributionSSG's check recognises only Red Hat Enterprise Linux as vendor-supported and requires Red Hat's subscription-manager. Rocky Linux and AlmaLinux are the operating system the customer chose; neither can satisfy a check that names Red Hat.None. If your accreditation requires a vendor-supported OS, use the RHEL image.
fapolicy_default_deny
Configure Fapolicy Module to Employ a Deny-all, Permit-by-exception Policy to Allow the Execution of Authorized Software Programs.		no STIG ID in the build recordCloud usability: you configure it after launchA default-deny fapolicyd allowlist blocks dnf, Ansible and every customer workload not in the list on a general-purpose image.Build an allowlist for your workloads, then set fapolicyd to deny-by-default.
network_configure_name_resolution
Configure Multiple DNS Servers in /etc/resolv.conf		no STIG ID in the build recordCloud usability: you configure it after launchThe rule wants two DNS servers in resolv.conf. On EC2 the VPC resolver is supplied by DHCP; the AMI owner manages DNS.Configure at least two name servers for your network, or keep the VPC resolver per your policy.
selinux_context_elevation_for_sudo
Elevate The SELinux Context When An Administrator Calls The Sudo Command		no STIG ID in the build recordCloud usability: you configure it after launchThe STIG's sudoers line (TYPE=sysadm_t ROLE=sysadm_r) makes sudo fail for the default unconfined_u login, so the image would have no working administrator.Map your admin users to staff_u/sysadm_u, then add the TYPE/ROLE sudoers line.
set_firewalld_default_zone
Set Default firewalld Zone for Incoming Packets		no STIG ID in the build recordCloud usability: you configure it after launchThe rule wants DefaultZone=drop, so every inbound packet no rule allows is dropped. Which services an instance offers is the deployment's; a drop default on a generic AMI blocks every port the customer's workload needs until they open it, and on EC2 the security group already filters inbound traffic before it reaches the instance.Allow your services in the drop zone (firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=drop --add-service=ssh, and each other service), then firewall-cmd --set-default-zone=drop and firewall-cmd --reload.
sysctl_user_max_user_namespaces_no_remediation
Disable the use of user namespaces		no STIG ID in the build recordCloud usability: you configure it after launchThe STIG itself says to set a non-zero value where containers run; rootless containers and sandboxes need user namespaces.Set user.max_user_namespaces=0 if the instance runs no containers or sandboxes.
rsyslog_encrypt_offload_defaultnetstreamdriver
Ensure Rsyslog Encrypts Off-Loaded Audit Records		RHEL-08-030710Remote log offload: needs your log serverThese rules send logs to the customer's central log server. The address, certificates and transport are the customer's; there is no log host we could point the image at.Point rsyslog (with TLS), auditd remote logging and/or systemd-journal-upload at your log server, with your CA.

Ensure Logs Sent To Remote Host		RHEL-08-030690Remote log offload: needs your log serverThese rules send logs to the customer's central log server. The address, certificates and transport are the customer's; there is no log host we could point the image at.Point rsyslog (with TLS), auditd remote logging and/or systemd-journal-upload at your log server, with your CA.
package_opensc_installed
Install the opensc Package For Multifactor Authentication		RHEL-08-010410Smart card / CAC: needs your PKISmart card (CAC/PIV) login needs a card reader and the customer's own PKI: their CA certificates, OCSP/CRL endpoints and certificate-to-user mapping. A cloud instance has no reader, and no CA or mapping we could ship is correct for any customer.
